newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila refiners suffer 1.3 bln pesos margins fall.
newsitem.headline: Manila refiners suffer 1.3 bln pesos margins fall.

text.p: The Philippines' three oil refiners said on Wednesday their margins have been reduced by 500 million pesos monthly since the implementation of an automatic oil price formula.

"The industry's margins are being eroded at 500 million pesos a month. What has happened since the automatic oil formula is that crude cost has increased more dramatically compared to Singapore Posted Prices," Oscar Reyes, Pilipinas Shell Petroleum Corp (PSPC) vice-president for finance, told Reuters.

The formula implemented last August 14 adjusts oil prices automatically every month based on Singapore Posted Prices. It is intended as an interim measure paving the way for full liberalisation of the energy sector.
Oil prices used to be adjusted every two months based on the landed cost of crude.
Reyes said average industry crude cost has jumped from $19.50 a barrel in August, to $20.95 in September and $22.40 this month.
An official from another oil company confirmed the margins cut which he said will amount to 1.3 billion pesos by end-October for the industry.
The Philippines' three major oil refiners are Petron Corp, Caltex (Philippines) Inc and PSPC.
Petron is 40 percent owned by Philippine National Oil Co. Another 40 percent is held by Saudi Arabia's Aramco and 20 percent by the public.
PSPC is a unit of the Royal Dutch Shell Group. Caltex is a joint venture between Chevron Corp and Texaco Inc.
